newsitem.title: UK: Railtrack down as Kleinwort repeats "sell".
newsitem.headline: Railtrack down as Kleinwort repeats "sell".

text.p: Shares in Britain's Railtrack Plc fell on Monday after analysts at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson restated a "sell" recommendation on the stock and regulator John Swift again attacked the company's investment record.
Railtrack shares were 12p lower at 369-1/2 by 1458 GMT.

Kleinwort analyst Chris Tarry said he had restated a "sell" recommendation because of continued worries about a windfall tax likely to be levied on Railtrack if Labour wins the next British general election, as well as signs that the company's regulator wants more powers over the company. "Political concerns are coming to the fore," Tarry said. "The Labour Party has reiterated what it's been saying, and it seems the regulator wants more tools in his toolbox."

Regulator John Swift told Sunday's Observer newspaper it was unacceptable that Railtrack had underspent its 3.5 billion stg maintenance budget by 700 million stg, but said to punish the company he had to wait four years for the first pricing review after privatisation.
